newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas, Shell sign gas deal.
newsitem.headline: Petronas, Shell sign gas deal.

text.p: Malaysia's national oil company Petronas on Tuesday signed a production sharing contract with Shell Malaysia Bhd, a unit of Royal Dutch Shell, to develop five gas fields off the East Malaysia state of Sarawak.
The total cost of exploring and operating the fields would be 14 billion ringgit, Petronas and Shell officials said at the signing ceremony.
The output from the five gas fields will feed the Malaysia Liquified Natural Gas plant in Bintulu, Sarawak.
Petronas president and chief executive Hassan Marican told reporters that Petronas and Shell would each have a 50 percent stake in the project.
He said the agreement will be enforced for 23 years from April 1, 1997 until December 31, 2020.
Shell Malaysia Bhd chief executive Megat Zaharuddin Megat Mohamed Noor said the cash flow from the project would be adequate to fund all the development costs required.

Shell orginally had held a 100 percent stake in the five gas fields since 1976 under a production sharing contract with Petronas, which allowed a 50-50 split in revenue after Shell deducted its costs.
